correctness.rationale: For every q>=3 the complete outgoing closed radius-two ball is {abc} union {bcz:z in A} union {cuv:u,v in A}; for a!=c, comparing abc and cbc gives singleton symmetric difference {abc}, forcing all q^2(q-1) endpoint-unequal words. For differing final symbols q(q-1)>q witnesses in Q_c; for same final but differing middle symbols q-1>=2 witnesses in R_{b,c} with <=1 potential collision; for same middle/final but different first symbols the forced self-word separates. q=2 additional differences force 010,101 and one of 000,111; direct exhaustive eight-vertex enumeration establishes exactly two size-seven optima. Reversing triples gives incoming-ball equivalence. Independently written enumeration reconstructed forward balls via two-step BFS and reverse balls via predecessor formulas for 2<=q<=7 and checked all forced singleton differences, all signatures and all 256 binary subsets; finite checks corroborate, not replace the all-q proof.
residual_risks: All-q proof is ordinary finite-word combinatorics, not a Lean/formal certificate; q<=7 computation does not prove infinite family.

value.rationale: The length-three radius-two case is the first natural n=2t-1 boundary excluded from established sharp directed de Bruijn constructions. The result settles an infinite family of alphabets, exhibits a sharp q=2 to q>=3 optimum-size transition, and uniquely classifies labeled optimal sensor configurations; neither a mere textbook deduction from the lower bound nor an arbitrary finite slice. It does not claim higher-radius or longer critical-length cases.
residual_risks: Priority not fully guaranteed; natural value relies on an exact first critical-boundary case, not a general higher-radius theorem.

final_claim: For each finite alphabet of q>=3 symbols, in the labeled directed de Bruijn graph B(q,3) with closed outgoing radius-two balls, the unique minimum identifying code is C_q={abc: a!=c} with exactly q^2(q-1) words. For q=2 the minimum is seven, attained by exactly the two complements of constant words 000 and 111; reversal gives the same statements for incoming radius-two balls.
